reviewer: Claude (Opus 5) review agent, independent of the extractor; no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the 70 records of the RFD4-Proteina batch (13 sources, 1 model, 6 configurations, 1 benchmark, 4 datasets, 6 protocols, 8 evaluations, 8 results, 23 claims) by a different agent from the extractor, against the extraction frozen at batch.jsonl SHA-256 f959706bc624873cfabc6db992dab16d8b61481422c2b17118e9c4fd97ceda8b. All thirteen pinned artifacts were re-retrieved on 2026-11-15. Twelve hashed exactly to their source record's artifact_sha256. The thirteenth, the RosettaCommons post, did not and cannot: the page embeds a per-request Akismet nonce, a per-request WordPress.com connect challenge with its own expiry and signature, and a 'generated in N seconds' footer, so two retrievals four minutes apart in this pass differed from each other as well as from the recorded hash. The post's recorded prose was diffed and is unchanged, and no value or performance claim rests on it; the finding is that the record's limitation claiming two byte-identical retrievals on 2026-11-15 cannot be right for this page, and it is recorded in this receipt rather than by changing a stored hash. Each of the ten archived gzipped artifacts was decompressed and hash-checked against the raw artifact_sha256, and each .gz against its archive_sha256: twenty of twenty matched. Three sources are recorded as mutable (the documentation site, the RosettaCommons post and preprint-versions.json) and each says so in its version and limitations; the two preprint PDFs are deliberately unarchived because they are refetchable at versioned URLs, and the post and documentation site are unarchived because neither states a reuse licence, both of which the records state. Both internal consistency checks were re-run independently and both hold: benchmarks/provenance.json declares summary.csv SHA-256 5c6d525d988d0df7fecb74396f86401c1ddb4c31fa83f00b357ba77d855d8a10, which equals the re-retrieved file, and preprint-versions.json declares version 3 SHA-256 b581fc10da53e94b263c36a7871906f10ba6559f993c02e08f8b3de6b1d0347e, which equals the 13,781,188-byte PDF served at the unversioned https://rfd4-proteina.org/assets/paper/RFD4-Proteina.pdf as well as at the versioned URL. npm run batch -- check-values does not apply to this batch and was not run: it reads JATS XML tables or a pdftotext -layout text layer, and the efficiency table is a Markdown table in a model card. In its place all eight results were re-read by a reviewer script written for this pass, review/check_values.py, which does not import or reuse extract/parse_efficiency_table.py: it finds the 'Measured design efficiency' section by its own heading, asserts the four printed header cells and the four row labels, requires each value to be printed to two decimals, splits comparator cells on the printed middle dot, and compares every stored printed_value, numeric_value, denominator, metric, unit, metric_direction and conditioning arm against that parse and against the archived benchmarks/summary.csv. Every card value equals its summary.csv unique_per_10_gpu_min times six at the printed precision, each row's attempts equals its targets times 200, and each cell's arm equals the dataset column of the summary.csv row behind it. The script also re-derived which summary.csv row each cell must come from, confirming independently that every RFD4 cell is the rfd4_proteina_high row and every comparator cell the highest non-RFD4 unique_per_10_gpu_min in that panel and criterion, so the card's own column headings are what was extracted. Because there are only eight cells, no sample was drawn: all eight were in addition read by eye against the model card, column assignment included. review/value-check.tsv records 8 of 8 in_cell with no mismatch. All 23 claims were read back sentence by sentence against the locators they name in the re-retrieved artifacts, including a pdftotext -layout text layer of the 101-page version 3 preprint for the four preprint-sourced claims. Two descriptive corrections were made before the batch was stored, so neither needed a records -- change: the Atomic Motif Enzyme conditioning text attributed to benchmarks/METHODS.md a statement that catalytic motif constraints are present in both conditions, which appears in none of the thirteen sources (the supplement's only statement about the degree of fixing is that AME compares partially to fully fixed ligand, not fully unfixed), and it was replaced in the AME protocol's allowed_information and description, in both AME evaluations' comparison.inputs and in both AME results' conditioning; and claim-inputs named coordinate groups as an annotation type, a phrase that occurs in the sources only in benchmarks/METHODS.md about how motif RMSD is scored, a file that is not among that claim's sources, so the value now follows the repository README's own list. Each previous value is kept in the review note of the record that changed. One vocabulary concept was added by this review, metric:passing-design-clusters-per-accelerator-hour in data/vocab/metric.ttl; unit:count-per-hour was added to data/vocab/unit.ttl by the coordinator at this reviewer's request, because unit.ttl is outside this reviewer's permitted edits. Both were accepted as genuinely missing rather than respellings of existing concepts.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude (Opus 5) agent, independent of the agent that extracted the batch, but not human scientific review. Transcription was checked against the pinned sources; nothing was reproduced, no inference was run and no value was recomputed from per-design data.

The RosettaCommons post's recorded artifact_sha256 is not reproducible by design, because the page embeds per-request nonces and a render-time footer. The hash is kept as published and the source record already marks the page mutable, but it cannot be used to show that the page is unchanged; the prose this batch cites was diffed instead.

Which checkpoint pair the efficiency table was measured on is not resolvable from the sources. The card's scope note says only 'the previous release pair', its checkpoints table has a 'Previous release' column naming one pair, and it separately names a superseded 2026-10-15 pair; benchmarks/METHODS.md says each cohort's exact schedule and checkpoint come from its own native config, which the packet does not publish. The configuration keeps checkpoint absent with reason conflicting. The review narrows it towards the 'Previous release' column but asserts nothing the sources do not state.

No checkpoint file was downloaded, so none of the published weight SHA-256 values on config-release-2026-10-19 was verified against the bytes; they remain transcriptions from release-checkpoints.json. The review checked the transcription, not the weights.

benchmarks/source_data.csv (1.5 MB of per-target rows) was not retrieved by the extractor and was not retrieved by this review either, so the passing-cluster counts behind the eight rates are unverified and numerator stays absent on every result.

The GPU model behind the GPU-hours is unreported in every source, so the eight values carry no hardware. A per-accelerator-hour rate measured on unnamed hardware is not comparable with one measured on named hardware, and nothing in the batch claims it is.

Version 3 of the preprint prints result tables this batch does not extract: S11 (training compute and clustered pass rates for the ablation reference, development-scale and release-scale models), S15, S16, S18, S22 (passing structural clusters per GPU-hour across six MCSA targets), S28 and S29. None of them prints any of the eight efficiency values, so no stored value needed re-sourcing. They are recorded as a gap for a follow-up batch and were not extracted in this pass.

Table S11's clustered pass rates for the release-scale model (10.6, 14.3, 12.1 and 3.5 per cent for the protein, small-molecule, enzyme and DNA target sets) are higher than the frozen packet's rfd4_proteina_high clustered rates (9.77, 8.74, 8.91 and 2.17 per cent) over the same 24, 77, 37 and 3 targets at 200 attempts each. That is consistent with the card's statement that the packet describes the previous pair, but it is a second author-reported figure for the same target sets on a different metric and belongs in the follow-up batch rather than being left unremarked.

benchmarks/summary.csv holds 52 method rows and 8 were taken into records. The remaining rows, including the low and medium thinking arms, the reward-guided search arms, nine further comparators and the looser historical disco criterion panel, were checked only far enough to confirm that each extracted cell is the row the card's column heading names.
The companion training-data dataset card was not retrieved or hashed, so the training data's licence is unverified beyond the model card's statement that it has separate terms.

The project page's live benchmark explorer was not extracted and no source record rests on it. Its coverage.csv at the pinned code commit labels its RFD4 rows a current October 19 cohort with different values, which the card itself says is expected of a live catalog against a frozen packet. It is a lead, not a contradiction, and no discrepancy claim was raised because the batch holds no record resting on it.
